summary: Wayne County, MO: a Conservation Commission tower site acquired in 1940; a 1963 fire, a 2022 auction sale for removal, and no confirmed word on what stands today.

facts.design: steel structure with an observation cabin at the top, about 110 feet overall (1963 survey description); an earlier 52-foot pole tower (1939-41 annual report)

events.note: Conservation Commission acquires 15 acres for a fire tower
Replacement tower put up at Cascade, per the fiscal 1953-54 annual report
Fire burns across the tower site and destroys about 55,000 hand-planted pines; the tower and other buildings are saved
Roof of the tower garage replaced, fiscal 1981-82 report
Tower sold at auction, total price $4,024.12; removal to be completed by March 31, 2023

notes_for_editor: Single source: the Central US Lookouts page, which quotes Conservation Commission annual reports and 1946 and 1963 newspapers. Those originals were not read. The 1963 steel-tower height is the only height in the sources, and the sources do not say whether that steel tower is the 1953-54 replacement, so height_m is the overall figure from the survey description. The record ownership is unknown, but both the 1945-46 manual and the 1963 survey say state land. Removal is not confirmed. Two leads were seen only as search snippets and not read in full: a GovDeals listing for Cascade (asset 2401) and a Missouri Conservation history Facebook post saying the Cascade tower came down; GovDeals returned 403. Check these before adding a removed status or any today sentence. Not on the cached NHLR or FFLOS Missouri indexes.
